text:
jessica-cs: Bluelloop just escalated — after a fw change at ~02:00 UTC their Private control plane connections started failing intermittently. Agents report API errors (agent->controlplane TLS handshake failures) and reconnect storms. They say rollback momentarily fixes it.
ana-support: Can you paste the exact agent error? any server logs from the customer side? if they opened a pcap that helps.
matt-ps: Customer provided this agent log snippet: `2026-03-17T02:12:34Z WARN control: tls handshake failed: tls: handshake failure` and on our control plane they see `tls: incoming alert 40 from 198.51.100.42` (same src IP). They also sent a tcpdump capture link (uploaded to their S3) — asked us not to share externally.
leo-neteng: Most common cause after fw change is TLS inspection/proxying. If a middlebox terminates TLS it will drop client certs (mTLS breaks). Also some proxies rewrite SNI or strip ALPN which is used by our control plane routing.
ana-support: Can we ask them to run an openssl check and tcpdump locally? Please provide commands to expedite.
jessica-cs: Sent requested commands: ```
# tcpdump on customer edge
sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/cp_handshake.pcap 'host 198.51.100.10 and port 443'
# openssl from an affected host
openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.com:443 -servername control.private.redwood.com -alpn h2 -msg -debug
```
matt-ps: They ran openssl and pasted the relevant part: ```
>>> TLS 1.3, Handshake [length 0003]
    16 03 01 00 2d
<<< TLS 1.3, Alert [length 0002]
    02 28
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
SSL alert number 40
---
```  They also see the server side closing immediately after ClientHello in the pcap.
sam-eng-priv: Alert 40 is generic handshake failure. Two things to confirm:
- Are they doing TLS decryption (MITM) on 443? If yes, that will drop client cert or present a different cert chain.
- Is SNI/ALPN preserved? Our control plane uses SNI to route to the right tenant control plane and ALPN for protocol selection; if those are stripped the server will abort handshake.
leo-neteng: On many Palo Alto/NGFWs we ask customers to add a decryption exception for our control plane IP ranges and set rule to 'No Decrypt (Passthrough)'. Example config snippet they can give to their netsec team:
```text
Rule: REDWOOD-PRIVATE
Source: <customer-net>
Destination: 198.51.100.0/24 (control plane range)
Service: service-https
Action: Allow
Decryption: No Decrypt (Passthrough)
```
ana-support: Also asked customer to verify NAT behavior — some egress proxies reuse source ports aggressively which can confuse our connection tracking on ephemeral sessions. tcpdump showed multiple connections reusing same src port in short bursts.
matt-ps: I pulled the pcap; I can confirm multiple SYNs with same src port and then a FIN/RST pattern. However the immediate server response in pcap is a TLS Alert 40 right after ClientHello bytes — looks like server rejected the ClientHello based on lack of expected SNI or because client cert handshake couldn't be negotiated.
sam-eng-priv: Other workaround if they cannot carve exception: terminate TLS inspection for that host range OR mirror the customer cert chain through the inspection device (rare). Best practice: allow passthrough for our control plane and add our control plane FQDNs to the allowlist so the proxy doesn't intercept.
infra-bot: automated: last_failed_handshake: 2026-03-17T02:13:22Z from 198.51.100.10, attempts=43
jessica-cs: Customer temporarily rolled back fw rule and confirmed stability for ~15min, then re-applied with a different policy and the failure returned.
leo-neteng: If they must keep the rule, ensure the firewall preserves TLS SNI and TLS SNI-based SNI forwarding, or add an allowlist based on destination IP (preferred). Also confirm the fw does not rewrite TLS ClientHello extensions (ALPN, signature_algorithms, supported_versions). If those are modified we will abort.
amna-support: (typo in previous) — asked them to run an s_client including `-servername` and `-alpn` and paste the full transcript. Also requested iptables/tcpdump when they toggle the rule.
matt-ps: Proposed resolution steps sent to customer:
1) Add control plane CIDR (198.51.100.0/24) to No-Decrypt / Passthrough on their NGFW.
2) If they use a proxy: add control.private.redwood.com to proxy bypass/allowlist and preserve SNI.
3) Confirm NAT source port behavior isn't collapsing ephemeral ports; enable port preservation or ephemeral port range expansion if needed.
4) Re-run `openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.com:443 -servername control.private.redwood.com -alpn h2 -msg -debug` and share transcript.

They applied step 1 and reported back: "connections recovered, mTLS handshakes succeed, agents re-registered" :white_check_mark:.
jessica-cs: Closing the escalation. Customer will follow up with their netsec to put a permanent passthrough rule. Marking internal follow-ups: add explicit docs note for support KB about NGFW decryption exceptions for Private control plane. :memo:
sam-eng-priv: I'll create a short KB entry and include the example Palo Alto rule and the openssl troubleshooting commands.
jessica-cs: Thanks all — leaving pcap in private ticket for SRE review later."
